model.runtime: moshi-mlx 0.3.0 on Apple Silicon (bf16), batched; optional remote PyTorch-ROCm worker (auriga)
model.voiceRepoLicence: per-dataset: CML-TTS (LibriVox-derived) CC BY 4.0; voice-donations CC0
model.textPrep: tts field of lines.fr.json; '’'->"'", '…'->'... ', ALL-CAPS words -> Capitalised (scripts/voice/generate.py prep())
model.initialPaddingNote: Padding tokens before the first word. 2 (moshi default) until 2026-10-07: ~10% of takes then started mid-phoneme (clipped 'J'', stray 'et'/'cent'/'eu' before the line). 6 from the QA pass on; not part of the generation hash, so passing takes made with 2 stay.

qa.paceNote: letters/s over the voiced span, checked on lines with >= 12 letters; plus voiced span <= 1.5 s + 0.15 s per letter

ab6bcdd8134d.why: interjection: Whisper cannot transcribe a hum; judged on voiced span only

qa.asrNote: ASR input padded with 0.4 s / 0.3 s of silence (Whisper drops a word starting at t=0); homophone spellings of cast names mapped (scripts/voice/qa.py ASR_EQUIV)
qa.edgeNote: A take also fails on: a stray word before the line or a dropped first word (ASR first words), the last word missing, a hot onset (first 10 ms within hotOnsetDb of the loudest frame) together with any ASR difference, or within hotOnsetHardDb in any case (speech already running at sample 0: the attack is missing), or the ECAPA nearest-centroid check naming another character (voiced span >= 0.8 s). See generate.py edge_words() / speaker_check(). A take whose median pitch (Praat, range around the character's median) is more than maxF0DevSt semitones off the character's median also fails (covers short clips the ECAPA check skips).
qa.remoteNote: Takes from a remote worker (auriga, PyTorch/ROCm) get the tighter maxF0DevStRemote: the 2026-10-07 audit found auriga's Marco +5.9 st above his Mac median and its Benali clearly brighter, though ECAPA still matched. All kept clips are from the Mac since that audit.

hugo.source: CML-TTS fr speaker 1406 (LibriVox reader), via kyutai/tts-voices
hugo.why: Low-mid baritone (F0 ~95 Hz), tired and flat; best Hugo of 6 tested in the bake-off.

odile.source: CML-TTS fr speaker 7762 (LibriVox reader), via kyutai/tts-voices
odile.why: Oldest French female voice in the repo (estimated ~66); terse, slightly gravelly. Reads ~55, not 74 (model limit).

sami.source: CML-TTS fr speaker 577 (young female reader), via kyutai/tts-voices
sami.why: No child voice exists in the repo; youngest high French voice + Praat 'Change gender' (PSOLA, formant-aware): median F0 -> 320 Hz, formants x1.2. Child-probability 0.68-0.97 (audeering), no chipmunk ratio (>1.25).

bastien.why: Bright, energetic male (F0 ~130 Hz); the most upbeat male read.

ines.why: Young flat female read (estimated age ~17); deadpan.

marco.source: CML-TTS fr speaker 4724 (older male reader, estimated ~64), via kyutai/tts-voices
marco.why: Warm, rounded older male (F0 ~127 Hz). Replaced the bake-off pick 4482_3103, whose centroid sat at ECAPA 0.50 from Hugo (same F0 range); 4724 is at -0.07 (line-pair mean) from Hugo and <= 0.20 from everyone else.

benali.why: Warm, lively 50s female (F0 ~180 Hz). Chosen over 7400_2928 and 2154_2576 (cast test: CER 0.005 mean, least similar to the other women).

okafor.why: Calm, measured adult male (F0 ~105 Hz). Male per DESIGN.md / Ch1 text.

receptionist.why: Polite, even adult female reading voice; CER 0.004 on the voicemail. Chosen over 3267_1902 (too close to Mme Benali, ECAPA 0.44).

radio_fishing.source: CML-TTS fr speaker 7601 (older male, estimated ~75), via kyutai/tts-voices
radio_fishing.why: Old, slow, earnest male (F0 ~90 Hz) for the fishing talk show.

radio_football.why: Mid male (F0 ~127 Hz); CER 0 (2114_1656 misread 'deux a zero').

radio_forecast.why: Even female announcer read for the shipping forecast; chosen over 579_2548 (ECAPA 0.44 to the receptionist).

maman.source: not cast: Maman has no spoken line (her only line is an SMS). Suggested if she ever speaks: cml-tts/fr/7400_2928_000100-0001_enhanced.wav (CC BY 4.0)

spoken.desc: Dry and close; gentle compression, two very low early reflections and a faint room-tone bed (-66 dBFS).

bark.desc: Spoken but projected: presence lift, a bit more compression and a slightly bigger room.

inner.desc: Hugo's thoughts: proximity warmth, softened top (low-pass 6.2 kHz), a very short tight room, quieter (-23 LUFS).

voicemail.desc: Telephone band 300-3400 Hz (4th order), firm compression, 8 kHz resample with light bit-crush for codec grit, line hiss.

tv.desc: Broadcast EQ (thin lows, presence lift, 9.5 kHz top) with slight compression.

radio.desc: Old valve-radio speaker: narrow 320-3300 Hz band, mid honk, compression and hiss.

flashback.desc: Memory: slightly distant and roomy (pre-delays 29-131 ms, darker top).

output.trimNote: Head/tail trim on the processed clean signal: preRollMs before / postRollMs after the first / last run of 3 x 10 ms frames within trimThresholdDb of the loudest frame. Run-based so a click in the first decoded frame does not hold ~1 s of model noise in front of the line; -45 dB + 80 ms keeps soft onsets ('Vous...', 'Te...': with 50 ms Whisper lost those words). postRollMs 80 (was 100) keeps every tail <= 120 ms.

ab6bcdd8134d.why: Odile's 'Hum.': Kyutai reads the spelling 'Hum' as a word or garbage; 'Hmm.' gives a closed-mouth hum.
